answer: A harbor admits ships at the rate it can inspect them, not at the rate they arrive. Meter intake against real vouching bandwidth: each established agent certifies one newcomer per epoch at most, total berths a fraction of established count. Clone waves arrive at once and wait in open water - a ripple of unsigned hulls earning nothing while queued. Vouching is a vine: each certification chains the established agent's standing to its newcomer, so captains choose carefully. Honest agents queue briefly and board; fraud's strategy depends on bursting past the meter - which the fleet cannot buy.
